name: Ascent

profile.address: North Point Parkway, Alpharetta, Fulton County, Georgia, 30009
profile.reading:
This building at 4905 North Point Parkway, at Kimball Bridge Road, in Alpharetta, Georgia was built in 2009 by BlackBerry (then Research In Motion) as a company data center, and its ownership history since then explains why this registry lists "Ascent" as operator even though the building no longer appears among Ascent's currently marketed properties. In February 2017, BlackBerry sold the roughly 40-acre property for $30 million to Ascent, a St. Louis-based data center operator, in partnership with TowerBrook Capital Partners; the deal included a partial leaseback letting BlackBerry keep operating space on site while Ascent took over the building, which it rebranded Ascent ATL1 and marketed for cloud and edge colocation tenants.

Ascent's ownership did not last: in 2022 the property was sold again, this time to a partnership between Lincoln Rackhouse -- the data center division of Lincoln Property Company -- and Principal Real Estate Investors. At that sale the building was described as 185,000 square feet on about 38 acres, with roughly 7 megawatts of live capacity expandable to 13 megawatts, and enough additional land on the site to support a new ground-up building of up to 30 megawatts. Under the new ownership structure, Ascent stayed on in an operating role -- continuing to provide facilities management, engineering, and construction services for the building -- while CBRE's Atlanta team and Digital Crossroad took over marketing and leasing to tenants. That arrangement is almost certainly why the underlying map data behind this registry still names Ascent as operator: Ascent runs the building day to day even though Lincoln Rackhouse and Principal, not Ascent, now own it, and Ascent's own current data center listings, which show only Toronto and Chicago facilities, no longer include Atlanta because it is not part of Ascent's owned portfolio.

No party in this chain of BlackBerry-to-Ascent-to-Lincoln Rackhouse/Principal ownership has published current tenant names, utilization, or a detailed cooling design for the building beyond the capacity figures disclosed at the 2022 sale, which is typical for a multi-tenant colocation asset that has changed hands through private commercial real estate transactions rather than public offerings. What is documented is the building's origin as BlackBerry's own facility, its 2017 conversion into third-party colocation space under Ascent, and its 2022 sale into a real-estate investment structure where Ascent remains the on-site operator rather than the owner -- a common pattern in colocation real estate that a facility's "operator" and its "owner" are not the same company, and that either can change without the other.

reading:
Ascent is a critical facilities services company rather than a colocation landlord. It was founded in 1998, works from 2350 Ball Drive in St. Louis, Missouri, and sells design, engineering, construction and, above all, the day to day operation and maintenance of data centres that other organisations own. Its Navigator platform is a customer portal for infrastructure management, and its staffing, round the clock operations centre and critical systems repair work are what it actually delivers on most sites. WESCO International, the New York Stock Exchange listed distribution and services company, announced the purchase on 31 October 2024 and closed it on 6 December 2024, describing Ascent as having more than 300 employees across the United States and Canada and 115 million dollars of trailing twelve month sales to 30 June, growing at better than 30 percent a year over three years. Trade coverage put the price at 185 million dollars on a cash free and debt free basis.

The registry holds one Georgia row for Ascent, and it needs care. The row is not a building outline but an industrial land use polygon roughly 300 metres on a side, on North Point Parkway in Alpharetta, in north Fulton County, tagged with Ascent as operator and carrying a link to a page on Ascent's former ascentcorp.com site for the Atlanta data centre it called ATL1. That page is no longer part of the live site. As it stood in 2023 it described ATL1 as a single storey hardened, LEED Gold building on a 38 acre campus, carrier neutral, with AT&T, CenturyLink, Comcast, Crown Castle, Fiberlight, Level 3, Telia, Verizon, Windstream and Zayo available. It gave three power numbers that are worth keeping apart. Up to 8.1 MW of critical power was available across two data halls, the site was described as capable of 30 MW of critical power at full build, and the utility service was two underground concrete encased 20 MW feeds. Only the first of those was capacity a customer could buy.

Ascent's current site lists two data centres, Toronto and Chicago. Atlanta, Dallas and St. Louis, all of which appeared on its 2023 locations menu, are gone from it. That is consistent with the business model, where Ascent's relationship to a building moves from owner to operator to former operator without the building changing hands in any way a map would show, but it means this Georgia row records a site the company no longer claims. The web address stored against the operator, ascent.co, now redirects to a domain marketplace listing rather than to the company, which is another reminder of how quickly a services operator's public footprint goes stale inside an aggregated registry, and why an unreviewed facility count built from map tags and old links overstates what an operator actually runs.
